title: Indian Market News Brief — 25 Nov 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Expectations of a smaller interest rate hike by the central bank and strong private equity investment in financial companies may support the market. However, sharp price drops in global technology stocks and fears of slowing foreign money inflows could create pressure. New rules offering guaranteed returns for gas pipelines provide positive news for energy companies.

stories.headline: A 50 bps jumbo rate hike can lead to financial stability concerns, hurt growth: Report
stories.summary: Economists at State Bank of India expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise interest rates by 0.25 percentage points. They previously expected a larger 0.50 percentage point increase. The economists said a larger rate hike could hurt economic growth and financial stability. The central bank rate setting panel meets from December 2 to December 4.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: A smaller interest rate hike means borrowing costs will rise less than expected, which could help banks and housing finance companies.

stories.headline: Dalal Street may face test from AI trade revival
stories.summary: Market experts stated that foreign investors moved money into Indian stocks during the recent sell-off in global technology shares. If global stock markets recover, foreign investors might reduce their money coming into India. This could slow down foreign capital coming into Indian markets.

stories.headline: PE/VC investments in India surge to USD 8.7 billion in October, highest monthly level in five years: EY-IVCA report
stories.summary: Private equity and venture capital investments in India reached 8.7 billion US dollars in October 2026. This is the highest monthly investment total in five years. Eight large deals made up 7.3 billion US dollars of this amount. Financial services attracted the largest share, getting 5.9 billion US dollars.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong private investment into Indian financial companies shows high confidence from large global investors.

stories.headline: PNGRB proposes 14% assured returns to attract investment in natural gas pipelines
stories.summary: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board proposed a 14 percent assured return for natural gas pipelines. The move aims to lower investment risks in gas transport infrastructure. The proposed rule also seeks to encourage lower costs and better pipeline use.

stories.headline: US markets slide, Asian markets rebound as Nvidia rally fizzles out
stories.summary: US technology shares declined as the price surge in chip maker Nvidia lost momentum. The Nasdaq index fell 1.5 percent while Nvidia shares dropped 4.7 percent. Meanwhile, Asian stock markets showed mixed trends, with South Korea's main index jumping 6.3 percent.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Price falls in US technology companies can make investors cautious about Indian IT stocks.

stories.headline: Shift in pension and insurance money to equities dampens long-term G-sec demand: RBI DG
stories.summary: A Deputy Governor at the Reserve Bank of India said insurance firms and pension funds are investing more money into stock markets instead of government bonds. This shift has slightly reduced the demand for long-term government bonds. The official noted this creates challenges for the stability of the government bond market.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: More pension funds buying stocks provides direct market support, but reduced demand for government bonds could cause wider economic concerns.

stories.headline: Stock market outlook today,25 Nov:Sensex, Nifty prediction-DJIA, S&P, NASDAQ, GIFT Nifty, Kospi, Nikkei, Taiwan cues
stories.summary: Indian stock market indices Sensex and Nifty saw sharp daily drops of over 1.7 percent recently. Investors sold shares across banking, financial services, and metal companies to take profits. Analysts noted that key support levels for the Nifty index sit near the 25,000 mark.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Heavy profit selling across key sectors shows weak short-term market sentiment.

stories.headline: South Indian Bank shares in focus as RBI approves SBI Mutual Fund to acquire up to 9.99% stake; stock up 612% in 5 years
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India approved a proposal by SBI Mutual Fund to buy up to a 9.99 percent stake in South Indian Bank. The approval is subject to meeting regulatory rules. South Indian Bank recently reported higher quarterly profit and income.
